headline: Eisenkot warns Netanyahu not to use security politically
dek: No new CEC count in-window: the standing figure remains 53 Netanyahu bloc / 48 Eisenkot bloc / 19 Arab parties at 85.6% counted (93% of ordinary ballots), ~600,000 double envelopes outstanding (1800-01). NEW reactions: (1) Democrats chairman Yair Golan urged the opposition 'change bloc' to reverse…
sources: Democrats chairman Yair Golan (X, via ToI); Gadi Eisenkot (via Al Jazeera, carried by Indian Express); CEC via ToI/Ynet
fault_line: Arab-partner government: kingmakers or red line? Golan says 65 beats 55; the rest of the opposition says it will not sit with Arab parties.

sections.what_happened: No new CEC count in-window: the standing figure remains 53 Netanyahu bloc / 48 Eisenkot bloc / 19 Arab parties at 85.6% counted (93% of ordinary ballots), ~600,000 double envelopes outstanding (1800-01). NEW reactions: (1) Democrats chairman Yair Golan urged the opposition 'change bloc' to reverse election pledges and ally with the Arab-led Joint List and Ra'am to oust Netanyahu: 'Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. Sixty-five is more than 55. That's how Israeli democracy works. Period.' (ToI). With the exception of the Democrats, the other opposition parties have said they would not include Arab parties in a coalition (ToI). (2) Eisenkot warned Netanyahu against using 'security for political needs', calling him 'a caretaker prime minister without a mandate or the people's trust' (Al Jazeera via Indian Express). (3) UNCONFIRMED single liveblog line: ToI liveblog reports the Eisenkot-led bloc is looking to replace Knesset Speaker Ohana with support of Arab parties -- not adopted beyond that line. TIMING DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: Ynet says double-envelope ballots are scheduled to be counted Wednesday evening; ToI/CEC say 'in the next couple of days' with further updates unlikely today. Official results expected next week (Herzog, via 1800-01).
sections.what_verified: ToI T3 (Golan statement, CEC count) + Al Jazeera T2 STATE-QA (Eisenkot warning, via Indian Express) = 2 families for the two reactions. Speaker-replacement line is single-family (ToI liveblog) and unconfirmed.
sections.what_disputed: Golan's '65' arithmetic assumes Arab parties vote with the opposition bloc, which the other opposition parties have publicly refused to do (ToI itself); Netanyahu's Likud remains the largest party (26 seats, Ynet) and Netanyahu claims a 'unique opportunity' with Trump on Iran (1800-06). The 56/48/16 balance remains unanchored (see 1900-11).
sections.why_matters: 65 vs 55: Golan's count says Netanyahu lost -- but the coalition math says nobody won. The Arab 19 decide everything, and the parties that need them refuse them.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW REACTIONS -- Israel election deadlock: Golan urges Arab-partner coalition to oust Netanyahu; Eisenkot warns Netanyahu not to use security politically; no new count (85.6% stands)

totw_analysis: Our read: 65 vs 55: Golan's count says Netanyahu lost -- but the coalition math says nobody won. The Arab 19 decide everything, and the parties that need them refuse them. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Arab-partner government: kingmakers or red line? Golan says 65 beats 55; the rest of the opposition says it will not sit with Arab parties.
